A.explanation: Both units are inverted in time. $1/T$ has unit $\text{s}^{-1}$, not $\text{s}$, and $b$ must balance division by $\text{m}$.

B.explanation: Homogeneity requires $c$ and $b/\sqrt{D}$ to both have unit $\text{s}^{-1}$, giving $c$ in $\text{s}^{-1}$ and $b$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: $c$ cannot have unit $\text{s}$ because it is added to $1/T$ which has unit $\text{s}^{-1}$, and $b$ is not $\text{m}^{-1}\text{s}$.

D.explanation: $c$ correctly has unit $\text{s}^{-1}$ but $b$ cannot be $\text{m}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$ because dividing by $\sqrt{D}$ in $\text{m}$ must leave $\text{s}^{-1}$.

hints: Start with the left side $1/T$ where $T$ is in $\text{s}$ - what unit must each term on the right side also have for the addition to be valid?
Use the homogeneity rule that $c$ added to $1/T$ must share its unit, and $b/\sqrt{D}$ must share it as well.
Work out the unit of $\sqrt{D}$ from $D$ in $\text{m}^2$, then rearrange $\text{unit of }b / \text{m} = \text{s}^{-1}$ to find the unit of $b$.
walkthrough: Write the equation with units: $1/T = b/\sqrt{D} + c$ with $[T] = \text{s}$ and $[D] = \text{m}^2$.
State the homogeneity principle: quantities can only be added if they have the same unit, so $[1/T] = [b/\sqrt{D}] = [c]$.
Check the table: unit of $b$ is $\text{m s}^{-1}$ and unit of $c$ is $\text{s}^{-1}$. This is option B.
